headline: Frankie — three days dark on the brief, and the company moved anyway. The "$300 Plan" is no longer a mystery campaign; it's the live paid motion, and a rebuilt watchdog now checks it every hour: $145 of $300 spent (48%), fourteen real leads now in — California, Texas, Nevada, Idaho, and as of this morning New Jersey. And you're already working them — the notifier screamed "SLA breach" on a lead named Charles and you fired back "no breach, he came in at 12:02 and I called him at 12:04." That's the good news. The bad news hasn't moved a millimeter: compliance is still 0/7, and the two items that actually bite — b3 (Texas telephone-solicitor registration) and b7 (your CA producer-license # on the creatives) — are the exact two the last ad account was banned for, and Texas and California are precisely the states you're now dialing. One lead even arrived stamped "no TCPA consent — call by hand." So the real revenue motion is alive and it is running on zero legal furniture. Today isn't "should we launch" — that's answered — it's: put the two numbers in place this week so the calls you're already making are papered, or scope the dialing to states that don't need them until they are. (Quiet second thread: the watchdog got rebuilt and thrives because it only touches cloud APIs — but everything that must write to your Mac is still dark. Meeting-ingest failed again this morning, no AM brief has shipped since Aug 28, and this PM is once again the only brief you'll get. The fix is the one the watchdog already proves: rebuild those as local tasks.)
